title: Precision-flip scan: Stability harness for FP16/INT8/INT4 quality vs perf
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Create a reproducible, automated harness that performs a precision-flip scan across FP16, INT8, and INT4 serving profiles and detects regressions in quality (likelihood delta / instruction-following degradation) and performance (tokens/sec, p95 latency). The harness must operate on representative production workloads (chat, long-context summarization, embeddings) and produce per-workload and per-sequence-length delta reports with statistical significance testing and an automated alerting rule for regressions.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness runs end-to-end for FP16/INT8/INT4 and emits per-profile CSV/JSON with metric buckets (tokens_sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, quality_metric_mean, quality_metric_std, token_efficiency).
2) Regression detector flags changes exceeding configured thresholds (e.g., >3% tokens/sec drop at p95, OR >2.5% relative drop in log-likelihood on held-out prompts) with p-value < 0.05 under bootstrap.
3) Reports include paired A/B comparisons and sequence-length stratification (<=128, 129-512, 513-2048, >2048).
4) Integration with CI: changes to quant kernels trigger a benchmark job and a blocking status if regression is detected for P0 release channels.
5) Dashboard artifacts (Grafana + CSV export) reachable from the Console QA project page.
test_plan:
- Build baseline model artifacts for FP16, INT8, INT4 using current kernel set.
- Define 3 canonical workload suites: chat-synth (200 prompts), summarization-long (50 docs with >2048 tokens), embeddings-batch (varied texts).
- Run 10 repeats per workload/profile under controlled instance types (A100-80GB, H100-80GB).
- Collect per-request traces (latency percentiles, token counts) and quality signals: per-token avg_logprob, instruction-following score (automated classifier), and a small human eval sample for high-risk cases.
- Run statistical comparisons (paired bootstrap) and publish HTML/JSON report.
- Wire alert rules: alert when token_efficiency delta < -3% AND quality_metric drop > 1.5% in the same workload bucket.
metrics_definition: p95_latency_ms: 95th percentile of end-to-end request latency (ms)
quality_logprob_delta: mean per-token log-prob delta vs baseline
instruction_follow_score: classifier score 0-1 measuring instruction adherence
token_efficiency: tokens_sec normalized by GPU utilization
implementation_notes:
Strategy: paired-run design where for every prompt we run baseline (FP16) then candidate (INT8/INT4) on the same instance type with warm KV cache and identical runtime flags. Use deterministic seeds for sampling where possible (temperature=0, top_p=1 for likelihood measurements; for open-ended quality tests use fixed sampling seeds to estimate interaction variance).
Trade-offs considered: realistic throughput tests require burst concurrency which can mask per-request latency regressions; to mitigate we run both single-stream latency traces and multi-stream throughput sweeps.
We will leverage existing quant-suite harness code but add: sequence-length bucketing, paired bootstrap test, classifier-based instruction-following metric, and CI gating that tolerates small perf losses if quality is preserved.
outstanding_risks:
- Human eval sampling rate may be too low to detect subtle instruction following regressions for INT4.
- Kernel nondeterminism across GPUs could inflate variance for p95; we will pin driver/kernel where possible.
- Emulating production traffic shape (prefix distributions, concurrency) is hard; false positives for regressions are possible if workload mismatch occurs.
